overview: Mirvac Group is a top-100 ASX-listed, stapled diversified Australian property group with over 50 years of history, integrating asset creation (development) and curation (ownership and funds management) across office, industrial, retail and residential/living real estate. The Group operates through three core segments -- Investment (a ~$10bn portfolio of office, industrial, retail and living assets), Funds (managing ~$18bn of third-party capital across wholesale funds, mandates and joint ventures, ~$24bn total assets under management) and Development (a ~$27bn commercial/mixed-use and residential pipeline). Mirvac concentrates its activity in Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane and Perth and is structured as a stapled security combining Mirvac Limited and Mirvac Property Trust (MPT).

business_model.summary: Mirvac earns recurring rental income from its owned investment portfolio (office, industrial, retail, and a growing build-to-rent/land-lease 'Living' platform), funds/asset management fees from ~$18bn of third-party capital, and cyclical development profits from residential (masterplanned communities and apartments) and commercial & mixed-use projects. Its integrated 'flywheel' model lets it originate, develop, lease, own and manage assets end-to-end, then recycle capital by selling stabilised or partial interests into its own wholesale funds and joint ventures with aligned capital partners (e.g., Australian Retirement Trust, Mitsubishi Estate). Target capital allocation is >70% investment (passive) / <30% development (active), with a target earnings mix of >60% investment / <40% development.

revenue_streams.name: Investment portfolio rental income (office, industrial, retail, living)
revenue_streams.note: ~$10bn portfolio (excl. co-investments/IPUC); FY26 like-for-like income growth 5.3%, 98% occupancy

revenue_streams.name: Residential development (masterplanned communities & apartments)
revenue_streams.note: FY26 Residential EBIT $233m, up from $179m FY25; 2,130 lots settled, gross margin improved to 24%

revenue_streams.name: Commercial & mixed-use development
revenue_streams.note: FY26 CMU EBIT $88m, up 91% on FY25 following FY23/24 negative revaluations

revenue_streams.name: Funds & asset management fees
revenue_streams.note: FY26 Funds EBIT $36m (Funds Mgmt $22m + Asset Mgmt $44m, less admin); $18bn third-party capital, up from $15bn FY25

business_model.customer_type: Mixed: B2B/institutional (office/industrial tenants, wholesale fund investors, capital-partner JVs) and B2C (residential home buyers, build-to-rent/land-lease residents, retail tenants)
business_model.geographic_mix: Concentrated in Australia's eastern seaboard and Perth: Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane and Perth

competitive_position.market_position: One of Australia's largest diversified, integrated property groups and a top-100 ASX company; a leading player in residential masterplanned communities and an emerging leader in build-to-rent/living, but a mid-sized player relative to pure-play office (Dexus, GPT) and industrial/funds-management giants (Goodman, Charter Hall) in their respective specialist segments.

moat_factors.description: In-house design, development, construction, leasing and asset management lets Mirvac control the full project lifecycle, capture development margin plus recurring fees, and is a capability few Australian peers can match at scale
Owning and managing assets for third-party capital partners (ART, Mitsubishi Estate, etc.) creates recurring, capital-light fee income and recycles balance sheet capital into new developments

moat_factors.factor: Brand and track record in residential/masterplanned communities
moat_factors.description: Over 50 years building communities gives Mirvac credibility with government partners (e.g., preferred developer status at Blackwattle Bay, Karnup) and buyers

moat_factors.factor: Balance sheet and credit rating discipline
moat_factors.description: Targets an A-/A3 investment-grade rating and 20-30% gearing, supporting lower cost of capital and resilience through cycles
Exposure across office, industrial, retail, living and residential smooths volatility versus single-sector peers, though it also dilutes best-in-class scale in any one segment

weaknesses: Sub-scale versus specialist peers in industrial/logistics (Goodman) and pure office (Dexus/GPT), limiting negotiating leverage and cost advantages in those sectors
Statutory earnings extremely volatile due to non-cash property revaluations (large losses FY2023-FY2024, large gains FY2021-2022 and FY2026)
Residential development earnings are cyclical and sensitive to interest rates, buyer sentiment and government tax/planning settings
Office portfolio still exposed to structural demand uncertainty (hybrid work, flight-to-quality bifurcation) despite gradual market stabilisation

growth_drivers: Expansion of the Living (build-to-rent and land lease) platform -- LIV Mirvac Fund targeting growth from ~2,200 to over 5,000 apartments medium-term, supported by strong rental market fundamentals (low vacancy, undersupply)

Growth in funds management -- third-party capital under management rose from $15bn (FY25) to $18bn (FY26), with new vehicles (e.g., retail venture seeded by East Village stake) and continued appetite from capital partners such as Australian Retirement Trust

Recovering commercial & mixed-use development earnings as major projects (Harbourside, 55 Pitt Street, Hunter Street East) progress and office market conditions stabilise with flight-to-quality demand

Residential pipeline restocking -- ~26,400 lots, plus newly secured masterplanned communities (Blackwattle Bay ~800 lots/$2.5bn end value, Karnup ~1,500 lots/$500m end value, Wantirna South ~1,750 lots) to sustain earnings into FY28 and beyond
Capital recycling and partnering (asset sales, JV sell-downs e.g. SEED Badgerys Creek Stage 2, Harbourside JV with Mitsubishi Estate) funding balance sheet strength and a $200m on-market buyback
Structural housing undersupply and population growth in Australia supporting medium-term residential demand despite near-term rate-driven softness

business.description: Earnings closely tied to market conditions, portfolio valuations and timing/quality of development delivery; economic conditions and internal capital allocation decisions both matter
Despite improving pre-leasing and flight-to-quality trends, secondary-grade office assets remain vulnerable to elevated vacancy and slower-to-convert tenant commitments

Momentum in the residential market has moderated recently due to geopolitical uncertainty, interest rates, tax setting changes and inflation, even though underlying fundamentals (undersupply, migration) remain supportive
Reliance on long-term capital and JV partners; market volatility can affect partner appetite and transaction activity
Reliance on diverse suppliers exposes the business to modern slavery risk, cost escalation, subcontractor insolvency and import/material risk; FY26 Middle East conflict disrupted fuel/shipping routes

financial.description: Ability to maintain 20-30% target gearing and secure debt/equity funding at a reasonable cost; weighted average debt cost guided at ~5.7% for FY27; targets A-/A3 investment-grade rating

Statutory profit swings materially with property revaluations -- statutory losses of $165m (FY2023) and $805m (FY2024) driven by ~$1.1bn of commercial (mostly office) writedowns, versus a $677m statutory profit in FY26 on positive revaluations across living, industrial and retail
Higher-for-longer interest rates raise financing costs, constrain transaction velocity/capital recycling and pressure cap rates/valuations across the portfolio

regulatory.description: Changes in planning laws, development approvals, zoning, immigration policy and broader government policy can delay or constrain projects
First mandatory AASB S2 climate-related financial disclosure lodged in FY26; net positive carbon (2030) and net positive water (2030) targets carry compliance and capex implications
Seventh Modern Slavery Statement lodged; ongoing supply chain due diligence obligations

macro.description: Interest rates, inflation, global economic volatility and regulatory measures affect valuations, access to capital and investor sentiment; FY26 characterised as a 'higher-for-longer' rate environment with subdued consumer confidence
Global conflict, trade protectionism, supply chain volatility and interventionist domestic policy described by management as permanent structural features rather than cyclical disruptions
Management flags AI as 'the most pervasive risk' in its profile in FY26, connecting to workforce, technology, cyber and real estate demand risk, alongside productivity upside

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Australian office markets are stabilising with rental growth resuming and pricing clarity improving, though tenant pre-commitments still take longer to convert; Prime-grade/well-located assets are outperforming amid constrained new supply. Industrial demand growth has moderated off exceptional prior levels but remains supported by Western Sydney infrastructure and low vacancy. Residential/living fundamentals remain structurally favourable (undersupply, migration, low unemployment) despite near-term softness from rates and tax settings. Build-to-rent is an emerging institutional asset class with strong rental market tailwinds.
macro_factors.cyclicality: High for development earnings (residential and commercial & mixed-use) and for statutory profit (driven by non-cash property revaluations); moderate for the passive investment portfolio, which benefits from long WALE leases and high (98%) occupancy providing earnings ballast
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High -- affects cap rates/valuations, cost of debt (FY27 guided average debt cost ~5.7%), buyer affordability in residential, and transaction/capital-recycling velocity across the sector

recent_developments.event: FY26 results: operating profit $508m (+7% on FY25), statutory profit $677m (vs $68m FY25) on positive revaluations across living, industrial and retail; operating EPS 12.9cps (+7%); distributions 9.5cps (+6%); gearing improved to 24.1% from 27.6%
FY27 guidance issued: operating EPS 13.2-13.4cps, distributions 9.9cps, residential settlements of 2,800-3,100 lots, weighted average debt cost ~5.7%, development returns target >10%

Commenced on-market buyback of up to $200m of stapled securities (through 2 September 2027), funded by cash and existing debt facilities, expected to be accretive to EPS and NTA; ~$105m (58.8m securities) executed by mid-September 2026

Secured Hunter Street East over-station development (Sydney, ~$3bn end value) in partnership with Coombes Property Group, plus new masterplanned communities at Blackwattle Bay (Sydney, ~800 lots/$2.5bn) and Karnup (Perth, ~1,500 lots/$500m)
Entered 50% joint venture with Mitsubishi Estate Co. Ltd for the Harbourside, Sydney precinct, sharing office/retail leasing risk
Sold down 49% interest in SEED Badgerys Creek Stage 2 into the Mirvac Industrial Venture (with Australian Retirement Trust), driving a 91% increase in Commercial & Mixed-Use EBIT to $88m
Board renewal: Janelle Hopkins (former REA Group CFO) appointed Non-Executive Director; Christine Bartlett resigned after 11 years
Stock underperformed the ASX 200 (down ~25% over the prior 12 months per Motley Fool reporting) before rallying ~6.6% to $1.86 on the FY26 results release

items.notes: Up from FY26 actual of 12.9cps; implies ~2-4% growth, contingent on stable market conditions
Up from FY26 actual of 9.5cps (+6% on FY25); implies further ~4% growth
Up from 2,130 lots settled in FY26
Return-on-invested-capital hurdle for development activity, consistent with ROIC > WACC framework
FY26 actual 24.1% (look-through 27.2%), within target band; supports A-/A3 credit rating objective
Funded by cash and existing debt facilities; management states it is EPS- and NTA-accretive

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Campbell Hanan described FY26 as 'a year of execution, with earnings growth of 7 per cent,' highlighting a strengthened balance sheet and confidence in the value embedded in the business via the buyback announcement, while flagging the need to balance gearing, capital drag from near-completion projects, and funding requirements for future development. Management noted residential market momentum has moderated recently due to geopolitical uncertainty, higher interest rates, tax setting changes and inflation, but that underlying fundamentals (migration, undersupply, low unemployment) remain supportive, positioning FY27 launches in Brisbane and Perth to capture demand.

bull_case: Statutory and operating earnings inflected positively in FY26 (operating profit +7%, statutory profit >$677m vs $68m) after two years of large non-cash writedowns, suggesting the office devaluation cycle may have bottomed

Integrated development-to-funds-management flywheel and diversification across office, industrial, retail, residential and living provide multiple growth levers and smoother earnings than single-sector peers
Structural undersupply of Australian housing and strong build-to-rent/land-lease demand support a large ($21bn) residential pipeline and growing Living platform (targeting 5,000+ BTR apartments)

$200m buyback plus disciplined 20-30% gearing target (24.1% actual, A-/A3 rating goal) signal balance sheet strength and management confidence that the stock is undervalued relative to NTA ($2.33/security)
Growing $18bn third-party funds management platform generates capital-light, recurring fee income and reduces reliance on Mirvac's own balance sheet to fund growth
bear_case: Statutory earnings remain highly volatile and dependent on non-cash property revaluations that can reverse quickly if cap rates rise again in a higher-for-longer rate environment

Residential development momentum has already moderated due to geopolitical uncertainty, interest rates and tax setting changes, creating risk to the ambitious FY27 lot-settlement guidance (2,800-3,100 vs 2,130 in FY26)

Office sector recovery is uneven -- Prime-grade assets outperform while secondary-grade space still faces elevated vacancy and slow-to-convert tenant demand, and Mirvac's portfolio is not purely Prime-grade

Analyst sentiment is mixed (consensus 'Hold' with price targets clustering around $2.00-$2.47, some well below others), and the stock has underperformed the broader ASX 200 materially over the trailing 12 months despite the FY26 rally

Elevated financing costs (~5.7% average debt cost guided for FY27) and reliance on continued capital recycling/JV sell-downs to fund the $27bn development pipeline create execution and refinancing risk if capital markets tighten
